newsitem.title: UK: Concern rising for Lloyd's insurance mkt - Chatset.
newsitem.headline: Concern rising for Lloyd's insurance mkt - Chatset.

text.p: The prospects of a collapse in profits at Lloyd's insurance market are growing as underwriters move into new areas and reinsurance rates decline, analyst Chatset said.

"All the signs are there for a market heading for trouble...We are seeing the beginnings of a return to the bad days when an underwriter thought he could arbitrage his book of business," Chatset said on Friday in its latest Lloyd's League Tables market review.
An increasing number of underwriters are looking for business outside their core markets, Chatset said. In the past, moving into uncharted waters has often led to losses.

The dangers are not as great as in the 1980s, when latent liability connected to the insurance of pollution and asbestosis risks fed through to the record market losses of the early 1990s, Chatset said.
However, premium rates have been falling for most classes of businesses since 1993, leaving many insurers exposed in the event of one or more major catastrophes.
Chatset said earlier that Lloyd's profits, which are announced three years in arrears, will be little changed for 1995 from 1994's 913 million stg, but will fall to around 700 million in 1996.
